title: Paid three ways: City, State and federal money in the same year
question: Which organizations drew City payments, a State grant and a direct federal award in the same fiscal year, and how much from each?
finding: 68 private organizations had all three in at least one of fiscal years 2023 to 2025, out of 313 that had a State grant and City payments; for 15 of them every one of the three came to $100,000 or more. The largest by their smallest leg: Wu Yee Children's Services (FY2024: City $1,643,167, State $1,967,344, federal $30,170,951); Mission Neighborhood Centers Inc (FY2023: City $18,189,159, State $1,500,000, federal $2,000,000); Urban Alchemy (FY2023: City $10,192,702, State $1,440,000, federal $2,000,000). The question is whether one cost was charged to two funders; nothing here shows that happened.
how: State grants are the California Grants Portal award files for State fiscal years 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25 (the only years published), kept when the recipient's name equals a City payee's after tidying; the same award posted by two State agencies is counted once, and awards to individuals are left out. City payments are the ledger total for the City fiscal year with the same number. Federal money is direct (prime) federal grants and contracts to the same name, placed in the federal fiscal year the award began; money the City passed on from its own federal grants is not counted, since it is already in the City figure. A year counts when each of the three is $10,000 or more. Public bodies are left out. Ranked by the smallest of the three totals.
limits: Three funders in one year is what a large provider is expected to have, and arts groups routinely hold a City, a State arts-council and a federal arts grant together. The State grant is often for a project in another county (the area served is given where it is not San Francisco), so it may have nothing to do with City-funded work. The three year labels do not cover the same months. A federal award is counted whole in the year it started. Matches are by name; 2 public bodies with all three were left out. Only an audit of the budgets behind each grant could show a cost charged twice.
